text.en: The inventory of word classes in Ainu is similar to that of Japanese ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--ainu-word-class-inventory-resembles-japanese⟧. Ainu has no conjugations or other inflectional morphological mechanisms that alter the basic form of a word ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--absence-of-inflectional-conjugation⟧. Syntactic criteria classify Ainu words into seven parts of speech: nouns, verbs, adverbs, prenominals, interjections, auxiliary verbs, and particles ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--seven-word-classes-classification⟧, whereas an analysis based on grammatical role and formal frame posits six major parts of speech ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--six-major-parts-of-speech-classification⟧. Kindaichi proposed classifying Ainu word classes according to whether words can combine with personal affixes ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--kindaichi-personal-affixation-criterion-ainu⟧, suggesting a division of Hokkaido Ainu words into those that combine with personal affixes and those that do not ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--kindaichi-personal-affixation-criterion-hokkaido⟧. In Shizunai Ainu, the lexicon is initially divided into three major categories: nominals, verbals, and clitics ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--shizunai-three-way-lexical-division⟧. Particles in Ainu fall into five functional classes: case particles, conjunctive particles, adverbial particles, sentence-final particles, and auxiliary verbs ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--nakagawa-five-particle-classes⟧. Historically, seemingly bound forms such as case suffixes, noun prefixes, and auxiliaries are independent words that assumed less independent roles ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--bound-forms-historically-independent-words⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語の品詞の種類は日本語と似ている⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--ainu-word-class-inventory-resembles-japanese⟧。アイヌ語には語の基本形を変化させる活用などの語形変化手段が存在しない⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--absence-of-inflectional-conjugation⟧。統語的特徴のセットに基づき語を名詞、動詞、副詞、連体詞、間投詞、助動詞、助詞の7種に分類する体系がある一方で⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--seven-word-classes-classification⟧、文法的役割と形の上での枠組みに基づき大別して6つの主要な品詞に分類する体系もある⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--six-major-parts-of-speech-classification⟧。金田一は語が人称接辞と結合できるか否かによる品詞分類を提案し⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--kindaichi-personal-affixation-criterion-ainu⟧、北海道アイヌ語の語を人称接辞と結合しうる語としえない語へ二分することを提案した⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--kindaichi-personal-affixation-criterion-hokkaido⟧。静内アイヌ語の語彙は、まず名詞類、動詞類、接語類の3大グループに区分される⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--shizunai-three-way-lexical-division⟧。アイヌ語の助詞は格助詞、接続助詞、副助詞、終助詞、助動詞の5つの機能クラスに分類される⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--nakagawa-five-particle-classes⟧。格接尾辞や名詞接頭辞、助動詞といった拘束形式に見えるものは、歴史的には自立性を低めた自立語である⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--bound-forms-historically-independent-words⟧。

text.en: Adverbs, adnominals, interjections, auxiliary verbs, and non-case particles have an arity of 0, whereas postpositional adverbs and case particles have an arity of +1, as seen in forms such as *pirkano*, *eytasa*, *ani*, *tura*, *tan*, *sine*, *iyairaykere*, *uwa*, *rusuy*, *pa*, *ta*, and *un* ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--arity-distinction-among-non-predicative-classes⟧.
text.ja: 副詞、連体詞、間投詞、助動詞、および格助詞以外の助詞のアリティは0であり、後置副詞と格助詞のアリティは*pirkano*、*eytasa*、*ani*、*tura*、*tan*、*sine*、*iyairaykere*、*uwa*、*rusuy*、*pa*、*ta*、*un*のように+1である⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--arity-distinction-among-non-predicative-classes⟧。

text.en: The predicate position in Ainu is invariably occupied by a verb phrase whose head is a verb or an auxiliary verb ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--predicate-position-headed-by-verb-or-auxiliary⟧. Verbs in Ainu can serve as predicates and take one or two personal affixes ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--verb-distributional-and-affixal-properties⟧. In Shizunai Ainu, verbals are defined as forms that can function as predicates ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-verbals-as-predicative-forms⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, the smallest verbal form capable of functioning as an independent word is called the basic form of the verb, exemplified by *komke*, *komo*, *tuye*, and *tuy* ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-verb-basic-form⟧. Unlike Japanese verbs, Ainu verbs make no formal distinction between conclusive and conjunctive forms ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--absence-of-conclusive-conjunctive-verb-distinction⟧. Inherently, the word *iomante* is an intransitive verb meaning 'to send the spirit of a kamuy' ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--iomante-inherently-intransitive-verb⟧. Forms showing semantic unity but grammatically behaving as two words are tentatively called separable verbs ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--separable-verbs-terminology⟧. Although limited in number, many separable verbs express basic meanings and are frequently used, including *kes anpa*, *ka opas*, *ka opiwki*, *ka ose*, *ka oyki*, and *par oyki* ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--separable-verbs-frequency-and-basic-meaning⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語の述語位置は常に動詞句によって占められ、その主要部は動詞または助動詞である⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--predicate-position-headed-by-verb-or-auxiliary⟧。アイヌ語の動詞は述語になり、1つないし2つの人称接辞をとる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--verb-distributional-and-affixal-properties⟧。静内アイヌ語において、動詞類は述語になりうる形式として定義される⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-verbals-as-predicative-forms⟧。北海道アイヌ語において、自立語として成立する最小の動詞形式は動詞の基本形と呼ばれ、*komke*、*komo*、*tuye*、*tuy*などがこれにあたる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-verb-basic-form⟧。日本語の動詞とは異なり、アイヌ語の動詞には終止形と連用形の形式的区別が存在しない⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--absence-of-conclusive-conjunctive-verb-distinction⟧。*iomante*という語は本来「（カムイの）霊を送る」という意味の自動詞である⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--iomante-inherently-intransitive-verb⟧。意味的には一語のまとまりを示しながら文法的には二語として現れる形式は、仮に分離動詞と呼ばれる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--separable-verbs-terminology⟧。分離動詞は語数が限られているが、*kes anpa*、*ka opas*、*ka opiwki*、*ka ose*、*ka oyki*、*par oyki*のように基本的な意味を表し頻繁に用いられるものが多い⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--separable-verbs-frequency-and-basic-meaning⟧。

text.en: Nouns are defined as elements that form noun phrases capable of serving as arguments, whether subject or object, to a predicate ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-nouns-as-predicate-arguments⟧. Nouns in Ainu do not serve as predicates, serve as verb arguments, and take at most one personal affix ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--noun-distributional-and-affixal-properties⟧. Ainu nouns exhibit neither case inflection nor grammatical gender distinctions ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--absence-of-case-inflection-and-gender-in-nouns⟧. In Refsing's analysis of Shizunai Ainu, nominals are defined as any free forms that cannot function as predicates ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-nominals-non-predicative-free-forms⟧. In that dialect, noun prefixes are strictly adjacent to their head nouns and restricted to specific noun subclasses, unlike adnouns ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--noun-prefixes-strictly-adjacent-and-restricted⟧. Noun suffixes in Shizunai extend nominals without altering their syntactic function or nominal status ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--noun-suffixes-preserve-nominal-status⟧. In the Saru and Chitose dialects, *okkay* is not used as an independent noun ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--okkay-not-independent-noun-in-saru-chitose⟧.
text.ja: 名詞は名詞句を形成して述語の項（主語や目的語）になりうる要素として定義される⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-nouns-as-predicate-arguments⟧。アイヌ語の名詞は述語にならず、動詞の項になり、人称接辞をとる場合は最大ひとつとる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--noun-distributional-and-affixal-properties⟧。アイヌ語の名詞には格屈折も文法性の区別も存在しない⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--absence-of-case-inflection-and-gender-in-nouns⟧。静内アイヌ語に関するレフシングの分析において、名詞類は述語になり得ないすべての自立形式として定義される⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-nominals-non-predicative-free-forms⟧。同方言において、名詞接頭辞は連体詞と異なり主要部名詞に密接に結合し、その分布は特定の名詞群に限定される⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--noun-prefixes-strictly-adjacent-and-restricted⟧。また静内方言の名詞接尾辞は、統語的機能や名詞類としての地位を変化させることなく名詞類を拡張する⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--noun-suffixes-preserve-nominal-status⟧。沙流および千歳方言では、*okkay*は自立した名詞としては用いられない⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--okkay-not-independent-noun-in-saru-chitose⟧。

text.en: Adverbs do not serve as predicates or verb arguments, modify verb phrases, and take objective personal affixes if any ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--adverb-distributional-properties⟧. Conjunctions, interjections, and adverbs are free forms that may function as adverbial adjuncts modifying whole sentences ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--free-adverbial-adjuncts-modify-sentences⟧. In Shizunai Ainu, conjunctions, interjections, and adverbs are free forms functioning syntactically as adverbial adjuncts that cannot serve as relational adjuncts ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--shizunai-adverbial-adjuncts-free-forms⟧. Adjuncts in Shizunai that are not subjects, objects, case-marked, or quotations are categorized as adverbial adjuncts to the predicate ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-adverbial-adjuncts-in-shizunai⟧. Negative and prohibitive words such as *somo* and *iteki* are adverbs that precede the verb phrase they modify ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--negatives-and-prohibitives-are-adverbs⟧. Postpositional adverbs express meanings similar to case particles but can also be used independently ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--postpositional-adverbs-independent-use⟧. Verbs converted into postpositional adverbs do not take nominative personal affixes ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--postpositional-adverbs-lack-nominative-affixes⟧. In the Saru dialect, the word *usa* is basically an adverb but can be used adnominally in repetitive coordination ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--usa-adverb-with-coordinating-adnominal-use⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, the adverb *sonno* does not take person affixes, in contrast to intransitive verbs like *sunke* ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--sonno-lacks-personal-affixes-unlike-verbs⟧.
text.ja: 副詞は述語や動詞の項にならず、動詞句を修飾し、人称接辞をとる場合は目的格をとる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--adverb-distributional-properties⟧。接続詞、間投詞、副詞はいずれも遊離形式であり、連用付加語として文全体を修飾することができる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--free-adverbial-adjuncts-modify-sentences⟧。静内方言における接続詞、間投詞、副詞はいずれも副詞的付加語として機能する自立形式であり、関係付加語にはなれない⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--shizunai-adverbial-adjuncts-free-forms⟧。また静内方言において、主語、目的語、格標示要素、引用のいずれでもない付加詞は述語に対する副詞的付加詞として扱われる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-adverbial-adjuncts-in-shizunai⟧。*somo*や*iteki*などの否定詞・禁止詞は、被修飾動詞句に先行する副詞である⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--negatives-and-prohibitives-are-adverbs⟧。後置副詞は格助詞と類似した意味を表すが、単独でも用いることができる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--postpositional-adverbs-independent-use⟧。後置副詞に転換した動詞は主格人称接辞をとらない⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--postpositional-adverbs-lack-nominative-affixes⟧。沙流方言において*usa*は基本的には副詞であるが、反復並列構文において連体詞的にも用いられる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--usa-adverb-with-coordinating-adnominal-use⟧。樺太アイヌ語では、自動詞*sunke*が人称接辞をとるのとは対照的に、副詞*sonno*は人称接辞を取らない⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--sonno-lacks-personal-affixes-unlike-verbs⟧。

text.en: Adnominals do not serve as predicates or verb arguments, modify noun phrases, and take no personal affixes ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--adnominal-distributional-properties⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, words that always precede a noun and function exclusively to modify nouns are defined as adnominals ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--adnominal-definition-exclusive-noun-modifier⟧. In Shizunai Ainu, adnouns modify nouns and occasionally nominalizers, precede the noun, and cannot occur in predicate position, as seen with *sino* ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--adnoun-distribution-and-modification-properties⟧, which distinguishes them from verbal modifiers like *pirka* ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--adnouns-distinguished-by-inability-to-predicate⟧. In the Saru dialect, the general adnominal *oar* functions both as an adnominal and as an adverb, appearing in expressions such as *oar*, *oar tek*, and *oar isam* ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--oar-adnominal-and-adverbial-dual-function⟧. In both the Saru and Chitose dialects, *sonno* and *sino* can function both as adnominals meaning 'real/true' and as adverbs ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--sonno-sino-dual-adnominal-adverbial-function⟧.
text.ja: 連体詞は述語や動詞の項にならず、名詞句を修飾し、人称接辞をとらない⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--adnominal-distributional-properties⟧。樺太アイヌ語では、常に名詞に先行し専ら名詞を修飾する機能のみをもつ語が連体詞と定義される⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--adnominal-definition-exclusive-noun-modifier⟧。静内アイヌ語において連体詞は名詞や場合により名詞化辞を修飾し、名詞に先行し、述語位置に立つことができず、*sino*がこれにあたる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--adnoun-distribution-and-modification-properties⟧。連体詞は述語位置に立ち得ないことによって、*pirka*のような動詞的修飾語と区別される⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--adnouns-distinguished-by-inability-to-predicate⟧。沙流方言において一般連体詞*oar*は連体詞としても副詞としても機能し、*oar*、*oar tek*、*oar isam*のように用いられる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--oar-adnominal-and-adverbial-dual-function⟧。沙流・千歳方言では、*sonno*と*sino*は「本当の」を意味する連体詞としても副詞としても機能する⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--sonno-sino-dual-adnominal-adverbial-function⟧。

text.en: According to Batchelor, there is no article in the Ainu language ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--absence-of-articles-in-ainu⟧. Particles in Ainu attach to free elements to express grammatical relationships ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--particles-bound-grammatical-relators⟧. In Tamura's model for the Saru dialect, an adverbial particle combines with verbal, nominal, or adverbial forms to yield forms of the same category ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--tamura-adverbial-particle-combination-model⟧. In Shizunai Ainu, the term restrictive postposition covers focus particles, restrictives, quasi-restrictives, comparators, and distributives ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-restrictive-postposition⟧. Also in Shizunai, clitics are bound forms unable to appear independently either as predicates or as isolated adjuncts to a predicate ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-clitics-bound-non-predicative⟧.
text.ja: バチェラーによれば、アイヌ語には冠詞が存在しない⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--absence-of-articles-in-ainu⟧。アイヌ語の助詞は自立要素に後続して文法的関係を表す⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--particles-bound-grammatical-relators⟧。沙流方言における田村の体系では、副助詞は動詞形・名詞形・副詞形と結合してそれぞれ同種の形式を形成する⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--tamura-adverbial-particle-combination-model⟧。静内アイヌ語において限定後置詞という用語は、取り立て助詞、限定助詞、準限定助詞、比況助詞、分配助詞を包括する⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-restrictive-postposition⟧。また静内方言において、接語類（クリティック）は述語としても述語の単独の付加語としても自立して現れることができない結合形式である⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--definition-of-clitics-bound-non-predicative⟧。

text.en: Interjections have no syntactic relation with other elements and form independent sentences on their own ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--interjections-syntactically-independent-sentences⟧.
text.ja: 間投詞は他の要素と統語的関係を持たず、それ自体で独立した文をなす⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--interjections-syntactically-independent-sentences⟧。

text.en: Chiri Mashiho's 1942 study was the first to propose that there is no need to distinguish verbs from adjectives in Ainu ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--chiri-first-proposed-no-adjective-class⟧. In general, there is no need to posit an independent word class of adjectives in Ainu ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--no-independent-adjective-class-in-ainu⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語において動詞と形容詞を区別する必要がないことは、知里真志保（1942）の研究において初めて提案された⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--chiri-first-proposed-no-adjective-class⟧。アイヌ語において独立した品詞としての形容詞クラスを設ける必要はない⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--no-independent-adjective-class-in-ainu⟧。

text.en: All intransitive (one-place) verbs in Ainu can in principle function grammatically as nouns without morphological stem change, as exemplified by *uwepeker* ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--intransitive-verbs-function-as-nouns⟧. In both Sakhalin and Hokkaido dialects, an intransitive verb or one-valence verb phrase can be used as a noun expressing a general concept ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--zero-converted-intransitive-nouns-express-general-concept-pan⟧, matching the behavior of unmodified intransitive verbs used nominally in Sakhalin Ainu ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--zero-converted-intransitive-nouns-express-general-concept-sakhalin⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, verb stems function not only as verbs expressing actions but also as verbal nouns meaning 'doing ...' ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--sakhalin-verb-stems-as-verbal-nouns⟧. In the Saru dialect, *tokapipe* is used both as a noun meaning 'lunch' and as a one-place verb ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--tokapipe-noun-and-verb-dual-function⟧. Also in Saru, the intransitive verb *sukup* 'to grow up' expresses 'life, living' when used nominally on its own ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--sukup-nominal-meaning-life⟧. In the Chitose dialect, the word *ekimne* can function both as an intransitive verb and as an adverb ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--ekimne-verb-and-adverb-dual-function⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語のすべての自動詞（1項動詞）は、*uwepeker*のように語幹の形態論的変化なしに原理的に名詞としても機能しうる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--intransitive-verbs-function-as-nouns⟧。樺太および北海道方言において、自動詞または1価の動詞句は一般的な概念を表す名詞として用いることができ⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--zero-converted-intransitive-nouns-express-general-concept-pan⟧、樺太アイヌ語においても無変化の自動詞が名詞として用いられると一般的な概念を表す⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--zero-converted-intransitive-nouns-express-general-concept-sakhalin⟧。樺太アイヌ語において、動詞語幹は動作を表す動詞機能のほかに「〜すること」を表す動名詞としても機能する⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--sakhalin-verb-stems-as-verbal-nouns⟧。沙流方言において*tokapipe*は「昼飯」を表す名詞としてだけでなく、1項動詞としても用いられる⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--tokapipe-noun-and-verb-dual-function⟧。また沙流方言において、自動詞*sukup*「育つ」は単独で名詞的に用いられると「生活、人生」を意味する⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--sukup-nominal-meaning-life⟧。千歳方言において、*ekimne*という語は自動詞としても副詞としても機能する⟦claim:nominal/word-class-inventory-and-diagnostics--ekimne-verb-and-adverb-dual-function⟧。
